prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” dentist — the right provider depends on your case, priorities (cost, speed, sedation, esthetics), and whether you need surgical placement, bone grafting, or a complex restorative result. For dental implants in Miami you’ll usually want either an oral & maxillofacial surgeon or a periodontist to place the implant and a prosthodontist or a restorative dentist with strong implant experience to make the crown. Many excellent specialists practice in Miami.

If you’d like, I can look up top-rated implant dentists near you — tell me your zip code and any preferences (insurance, budget, desire for sedation, one‑visit implants, etc.). Meanwhile, here’s how to pick the best provider and questions to ask:

What to look for
- Specialty and training: oral & maxillofacial surgeon, periodontist, or prosthodontist for complex cases. Check additional implant fellowships/certifications (AAID, ICOI).
- Experience: number of implants placed and experience with cases like yours (single tooth, full-arch, bone grafting).
- Technology: in-office CBCT (3D imaging), digital planning or guided surgery, intraoral scanner.
- Team approach: surgeon and restorative dentist coordinate care (same practice or tight collaboration).
- Before/after photos and patient references.
- Clear treatment plan, timeline, and written cost estimate including implant, abutment, crown, and any grafting.
- Warranty/aftercare and emergency availability.

Questions to ask at consultation
- How many implants have you placed? How many similar to my case?
- Will you place and restore the implant, or will you refer the crown to another dentist?
- Do you use CBCT and guided surgery? Can you show my planned placement?
- What implant system/brand do you use?
- What are the risks and expected complications?
- What's the total cost, and what does it include (imaging, grafts, temporary crown)?
- Do you offer sedation/sleep dentistry?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient testimonials?

Where to search and verify
- AAOMS (American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons) directory
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) or ICOI directories
- ADA Find-a-Dentist
- Local reviews: Google Maps, Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Yelp — read multiple reviews
- Ask your general dentist or local dental school (University of Miami) for referrals

Practical notes
- Typical single-tooth implant (placement + abutment + crown) in the U.S. can range roughly $2,000–$5,000+ depending on grafting and location; full-arch cases cost much more.
- Complex cases (bone grafts, sinus lifts, immediate load/all‑on‑x) should be handled by experienced specialists.

If you want, tell me your Miami zip code and any preferences and I’ll compile a short list of highly rated implant specialists and what to check for each.
